> Dual-agent review by **Claude** and **Codex**.
> Requested by @lolipopshock.

## Summary of PR/Issue
- PR #405 converts simple Sepo issue templates to Markdown for a more mobile-friendly GitHub issue composer flow.
- It adds `ask-sepo.md`, replaces the install YAML form with `install-sepo.md`, keeps `agent-goal.yml` unchanged, and updates install-template links in README/docs.
- The linked issue #395 explicitly accepted Markdown templates for simple Sepo commands, with the expectation that Sepo can ask for missing install info.
- The implementation mostly matches that direction, but the new install template includes a parseable placeholder that changes install-routing behavior.

## Review
The core conversion is sound and rubric-aligned, but the install template has one actionable behavioral regression. Both code reviewers identified the placeholder URL issue; the rubric review passed and did not add blocking concerns.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Install template placeholder resolves as a real target | BLOCKING | `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/install-sepo.md` includes `https://github.com/owner/repo`, which the install resolver treats as `owner/repo` if the template is submitted unedited. This bypasses the intended missing-target clarification path from #395 and the current test asserts the unsafe placeholder. |

## Progress
- PR already implements the requested Markdown `Ask Sepo` and `Install Sepo` templates.
- `agent-goal.yml` remains unchanged, matching the linked issue discussion.
- README and docs links were updated from `install-sepo.yml` to `install-sepo.md`.
- Existing inline comments and review threads were empty before synthesis; I posted one new inline comment on `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/install-sepo.md` line 11.

## Issue Details
<details>
<summary>Install template placeholder resolves as a real target</summary>

**Cause:** Markdown template body text is submitted as the issue body. The line [`https://github.com/owner/repo`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/3acb7904723b7120a3fbddedd9d3f5ca08245bd5/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/install-sepo.md#L11) is therefore parsed by `resolveInstallTargetFromText` as a clear install target, `owner/repo`.

**Candidate solutions:** Replace the default body with non-parseable guidance, such as `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>` or an instruction-only comment. Update `envelope.test.ts` or nearby install-target coverage to assert that the default install template body resolves as `missing`, not `clear`.

**Comments:** Codex treated this as blocking; Claude labeled it warning/minor unless maintainers require the missing-info guarantee. The linked issue explicitly mentions Sepo asking for missing info, so this synthesis treats the regression as blocking.

</details>

## Recommended Next Step
`FIX_PR`: the remaining work is a small, concrete branch change that an automated fix-pr pass can safely make.

## Final Verdict
`NEEDS_REWORK`

## Action Items
- [ ] Replace the parseable install placeholder with non-parseable guidance so an untouched install template body resolves as missing.
- [ ] Add or update test coverage so the default install Markdown body cannot regress to a clear `owner/repo` target.

The local checkout is still on the base state, but the PR diff has the new `.md` contents. I have enough to answer the specific behavior question now.Yes. In a Markdown issue template, the body text is inserted literally into the GitHub issue composer. So the current line:

```md
https://github.com/owner/repo
```

would show up to users, and if they submit without replacing/deleting it, Sepo can parse it as a real target repo: `owner/repo`.

For this template I’d avoid a parseable placeholder. Better options:

```md
<!-- Paste the public GitHub repository URL here. -->
```

or:

```md
https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>
```

The first option is safest because an untouched template should make Sepo ask for the missing target instead of trying to install into `owner/repo`.
